ALL INVENTED TEST DATA. Synthetic candidate DATA-001; no real person, school, employer, contact details, repository or applicant is represented. Every project, competition, date and metric below is fictional fixture content, NOT actual achievements or release measurements.

Profile: Final-year undergraduate with generic statistics and computing coursework. Focus on SQL, Tableau, payment operations and product analytics. This is a deliberately high-skill-match test persona, not evidence of US eligibility or a real application.
Skills: PostgreSQL SQL, joins/window functions/CTEs, data grain, Tableau calculated fields and dashboards, Python pandas, reconciliation, settlement, product funnels/cohorts, experiment design, documentation and stakeholder communication.

Invented project A: MerchantPulse acquiring analytics, 2025-2026. Designed separate transaction, settlement and merchant tables and generated a fictional 120,000-row dataset containing duplicate webhooks, delayed settlements and refunds. Used transaction_id plus event_id deduplication and defined approval rate with eligible authorization attempts as denominator, settlement lag in hours, and reconciliation break rate by business day and currency. Avoided joining multiple refund rows directly into transaction-level KPI aggregates.
Built a Tableau dashboard with merchant segment, channel and date filters. Documented pending versus failed versus completed settlements and used a reporting watermark for late-arriving records. A reconciliation query performed a full outer join on transaction reference and currency, classified missing-side and amount-mismatch exceptions, and retained an audit trail.
Invented test metrics: 36 SQL fixture checks for null IDs, duplicates, join fan-out, currency mismatches and timezone boundaries; 100 percent detection of 40 deliberately seeded reconciliation exceptions. These are fictional test-persona numbers, not release evaluation results.

Invented project B: ActivateLab product adoption experiment, 2026. Defined activated merchant as completing a first successful transaction within seven days after onboarding. Assigned fictional merchants to groups using a stable hash, checked sample-ratio mismatch, and tracked adoption alongside refund rate and support burden as guardrails. A fictional 2,000-merchant exercise observed 42 percent versus 46 percent activation; the candidate reported confidence intervals and explicitly did not claim significance without checking sample size and assumptions.
Automated SQL-to-Tableau refresh checks in a Python script with date bounds, row-count checks and idempotent outputs. Invented test metric: reduced a fictional classroom manual refresh from 40 to 12 minutes. No real payment data, customer impact or production experiment is claimed.

Invented competition: Fictional Campus Payment Analytics Cup, 2026. Four fictional teammates; candidate owned KPI definitions and exception analysis. Fictional third place among 15 fictional teams. Competition and award are invented.
Communication: Prepared a one-page metric dictionary and explained why a launch-week approval-rate change could be merchant-mix rather than a product improvement. Reviewed ambiguous business rules with fictional operations and product teammates.
Limits: Only synthetic financial data. No real regulated payment operations, employer, certificate or measured business achievement. Do not introduce new projects, employment or quantified success while answering.
